thread:
lina: Heads-up: tomorrow 09:00 UTC were activating new org-level IAM guardrails. New service accounts will get permission boundaries and org policy will block user-managed long-lived keys on creation. Existing keys need rotation or an exemption. :rotating_light:

aj: Does this change apply to customer-managed identities in Dedicated/Private?
lina: No, only Redwood org-managed identities. Well publish guidance for customer-managed setups.

chen: Concrete actions for infra owners?
lina: 1) Inventory SAs with user-managed keys. 2) Migrate to workload identity / OIDC or STS. 3) Stop automations that download JSON keys. 4) Request temporary exemptions with a ticket.

Tom: Will Terraform modules be updated?
lina: Yes  new module v2.1.0 adds a default permission boundary; opt-out requires security ticket. Release today 16:00 UTC.

sarah: Jenkins runners still using JSON keys  plan?
lina: Migrate to workload identity federation or credential helpers. Jenkins migration doc: https://internal.redwood/infra/ci-migrate - tag infra-oncall if you need help.

infra-oncall-bot: Note: soft-audit for 48h after enforcement start, then hard block. Noncompliant SAs will generate eng-security tickets.

lina: Were attaching an ownership CSV to the ticket. Assign owners for any unowned SAs by EOD tomorrow.

chen: Can we get a short runbook for rotating keys safely?
lina: On it  runbook will be posted to the ticket by 17:00 UTC.

infra-oncall-bot: Initial audit flagged 27 SAs for review. Ticket: https://internal.redwood/engsec/tickets/RED-4301

lina: Enforcement start: 2024-11-19T09:00:00Z. If you hit a breakage open a ticket titled "iam-guardrails-incident" and @infra-oncall will triage. Closing thread.
